gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many minutes each candidate actually runs a cooktop at full 1,800 W, or what it costs per usable watt-hour. Using reviewers' measured AC output, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 gives about 68 minutes at $0.44 per usable Wh. The BLUETTI AC180 and the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 give about 30–32 minutes at about $0.58 per usable Wh. A 2 kW load overheated the C1000 Gen 2 after 26 minutes.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's own answer, bluettipower.com/pages/ac200l (cited), solarwaypoint.com's C2000 Gen 2 vs AC200L vs DELTA 2 Max page, and itechguides.com's 2,048 Wh roundup. ChatGPT's cooking times (for example 60–70 minutes at 1,500 W for 2,000 Wh) assume a flat 85% efficiency. The BLUETTI AC200L page assumes 90% depth of discharge times 90% inverter efficiency and never mentions cooktops. Solarwaypoint lists no prices, no usable capacity and no cooking runtime. Itechguides computes $/Wh from rated capacity only and says cooking runtime 'cannot be derived'. None of these pages uses a measured usable-Wh figure, none gives cost per usable Wh, and none mentions the C1000 Gen 2 overheating under a 2 kW load. I could not open the cited unpluggedwatts.com page (SSL certificate error), so it is not part of this comparison.
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the pick. It gives the most minutes at 1,800 W (about 68) and the lowest cost per usable Wh ($0.44). The 1 kWh, 1,800–2,000 W units give about half an hour at full power, which is one quick meal, and cost about 30% more per usable Wh. The Anker C1000 Gen 2 should drop from 'Yes, small headroom' to 'at its limit', because The Technology Man saw it overheat at 2 kW after 26 minutes.
